```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)

library(tidyverse)
library(tidytuesdayR)
library(janitor)
library(tinytable)

# Download TidyTuesday data
tuesdata <- tidytuesdayR::tt_load("2026-05-05")

# Find what datasets are present for this week
names(tuesdata)

# Name datasets
food <- tuesdata$food_beverages
textiles <- tuesdata$textiles
transport <- tuesdata$transport

readme(tuesdata)
```

```{r graph, warning=FALSE}
library(scales)
textiles_selected <- textiles %>%
  filter(year >= 1900) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(
      cotton_yarn,
      flock_yarn,
      cotton_textiles,
      flock_textiles,
      other_textiles,
      raw_silk
    ),
    names_to = "textile_type",
    values_to = "production"
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(production)) %>%
  mutate(
    textile_type = case_when(
      textile_type == "cotton_yarn" ~ "Cotton yarn",
      textile_type == "flock_yarn" ~ "Flock yarn",
      textile_type == "cotton_textiles" ~ "Cotton textiles",
      textile_type == "flock_textiles" ~ "Flock textiles",
      textile_type == "other_textiles" ~ "Other textiles",
      textile_type == "raw_silk" ~ "Raw silk"
    )
  )
```


```{r more graph, warning=FALSE}
ggplot(
  textiles_selected,
  aes(x = year, y = production, color = textile_type)
) +
  annotate(
    "rect",
    xmin = 1939,
    xmax = 1945,
    ymin = -Inf,
    ymax = Inf,
    alpha = 0.18,
    fill = "#5A3E36"
  ) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9, alpha = 0.95) +
  geom_point(size = 1.2, alpha = 0.75) +
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = 1942,
    y = max(textiles_selected$production, na.rm = TRUE) * 0.95,
    label = "Sharp wartime\ndisruption",
    size = 3,
    fontface = "bold",
    color = "#3B2F2F"
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = comma
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Italian Textile Production After 1900",
    subtitle = "Cotton, flock, other textiles, and raw silk production show a sharp mid-century disruption",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Production in tons",
    color = NULL,
    caption = "Source: TidyTuesday 2026-05-04| ISTAT historical industrial production"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "#F6EFE7", color = NA),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "#F6EFE7", color = NA),
    panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "#D8C8B8", linewidth = 0.35),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(
      face = "bold",
      size = 22,
      color = "#2E2520"
    ),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(
      size = 12.5,
      color = "#5C5048",
      margin = margin(b = 12)
    ),
    axis.title.y = element_text(
      color = "#3B2F2F",
      face = "bold"
    ),
    axis.text = element_text(color = "#3B2F2F"),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.text = element_text(size = 11, color = "#3B2F2F"),
    plot.caption = element_text(
      color = "#6E625D",
      size = 9,
      hjust = 1
    )
  )



ggplot(
  textiles_selected,
  aes(x = year, y = production, color = textile_type)
) +
  annotate(
    "rect",
    xmin = 1939,
    xmax = 1945,
    ymin = -Inf,
    ymax = Inf,
    alpha = 0.18,
    fill = "#5A3E36"
  ) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_point(size = 1.0, alpha = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~ textile_type, scales = "free_y", ncol = 2) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma) +
  labs(
    title = "The Shock to Italian Textile Production",
    subtitle = "Selected textile industries after 1900, with the 1939–1945 disruption highlighted",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Production in tons",
    caption = "Source: TidyTuesday 2026-05-04| ISTAT historical industrial production"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "#F6EFE7", color = NA),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "#F6EFE7", color = NA),
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "#E8D8C8", color = NA),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", color = "#2E2520"),
    panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "#D8C8B8", linewidth = 0.35),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 21, color = "#2E2520"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12, color = "#5C5048"),
    axis.text = element_text(color = "#3B2F2F"),
    legend.position = "none",
    plot.caption = element_text(color = "#6E625B", size = 9, hjust = 1)
  )
```
